newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - INDONESIAN NEWSPAPERS - AUGUST 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - INDONESIAN NEWSPAPERS - AUGUST 13.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on August 13. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The armed forces socio-political chief Lieutenant-General Syarwan Hamid has said the military is not suspicious of ousted Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) leader Megawati Sukarnoputri as she has always been constitutional in her actions.
District officials in Indonesia's second city of Surabaya will be armed with tear gas under a plan by the East Java government.
President Suharto urged Indonesians to acquire technological know-how as building factories alone would not be enough to secure the country's survival in the era of technology.

Analysts have warned the $690 million syndicated loan from domestic banks to would-be carmaker PT Timor Putra Nasional to construct a factory could turn sour and become a bad debt because of low sales of its Timor car, currently imported from South Korea.

An Indonesian business consortium has started construction of a 558-metre tower in the centre of Jakarta costing some $560 million which will contain a revolving restaurant and viewing deck as well as be used as a communications tower.

Indonesia's Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) said the country's inflation rate this year was likely to be higher than the previous forecast of six percent if an ongoing drought lasts longer and the negative impacts could not be contained.
